turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on back. I'll grab vitals before the doctor gets in. Can you step up here for me?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She wiggles on the scale. Parking was a nightmare, we almost turned around.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): You're all set. Temperature ninety-eight point four, pulse ninety-two, oxygen ninety-eight percent, respirations twenty, and blood pressure one hundred over sixty-four.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): He should be along in a minute.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen keeps spinning. One second. Okay. What brings you in?
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's her cough. It came on with the flu and it just will not quit.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hold on, I opened the wrong tab. Sorry. How long has that cough been going?
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Six weeks. She had the flu first, fever and the whole thing, and the cough started as that was fading and it stayed.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Six weeks. One more time? The note field just cleared itself.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Six weeks. And it's worse at night. She coughs until she wakes herself up.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Nighttime is bad.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nighttime. Any fever now?
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not anymore. She was hot during the flu, but that part is gone.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Honey, have you lost any weight?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): How's she eating?
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Pretty much her usual. She's picky. Yesterday it was crackers in front of a cartoon and that was lunch. She's five, so.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is she short of breath at all?
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Just the cough. She did the swings at the park yesterday like she was fine.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): When you cough, does stuff come up? Any blood?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No blood. Sometimes a little clear mucus in the morning.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She hasn't said anything hurts.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you traveled recently, or been around anyone with tuberculosis?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay, no travel, no TB contacts. I'm typing it now before this thing freezes on me.

[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually, hang on. We didn't travel, we stayed in town, but her cousin Jordan came over for the birthday. My sister said the clinic thought his cough might be TB. Nobody ever told us if it was or wasn't.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, a warning just covered the screen. Who was sick?
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Jordan, the cousin. Possible TB, not confirmed, and she was around him at our house. Maybe three weeks ago, maybe four, I don't know, the weeks run together.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): He was on the couch.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. I am not going to put a name on this cough. Big breath for me.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Like this?
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. Lungs are clear, no wheeze, no crackles. Throat isn't red. Ears look fine.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So we're okay?
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): I didn't say it was nothing. Clear just means I can't hear a cause. Hang on, the order box blanked out again.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): My pants are loose.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): What was that? I was looking at the screen.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): My pants are loose. Mom ties them.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): You said you hadn't lost weight. Now the pants are looser?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. They're just loose.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I did cinch the drawstring, last weekend. I figured she was between sizes, not losing weight. She won't stand on our scale at home, so I don't have a number.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did you notice the clothes getting loose?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Maybe a couple of weeks. I'm only guessing.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): What is she taking for medicines?

[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Loratadine, five milligrams, every morning, her nose is still runny. She finished the Tamiflu with the flu, thirty milligrams twice a day for five days. That's long done.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Loratadine five milligrams each morning, oseltamivir stopped. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, none.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll go with no known medicine allergies, from Mom. I'm going to order a chest X-ray today.
[SEG0054] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Can they do it here?
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Downstairs, yes. If the cough has not settled, we might do a CT. Not ordering that today.
[SEG0056] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let's see her back in two weeks. If she's working harder to breathe, or there's blood, come in sooner, don't wait on me.
[SEG0058] person_1 (NURSE): I can walk you down to radiology. Elevator's cranky, just so you know.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Possible TB was in the cousin, not family history of the patient.
Transcript specifies no known medicine allergies, not all allergies.

omissions.text: Possible tuberculosis exposure was present, not absent: family member reported cousin Jordan had possible TB (not confirmed) and the patient was around him at their house about 3-4 weeks ago, so the recorded negative finding of no TB contacts is wrong.

Weight loss was denied initially by the patient, then questioned because clothes/pants had been looser for about a couple of weeks; family member was unsure if this represented actual weight loss and had no home scale measurement.
Negative finding: no current fever now.
Negative finding: appetite/eating is pretty much usual.
Negative finding: no confirmed medication allergies / no known medicine allergies.
